en.name: Madeira vine leaves
en.summary: Madeira vine leaves are the thick, slightly slippery heart-shaped leaves of Anredera cordifolia, stir-fried with sesame oil and ginger in Taiwan. No figure is published for them, so treat them like tender salad greens: about 2–4 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: These leaves have no useful room-temperature life. They are mucilaginous — the slipperiness that makes them pleasant in a wok is a soluble gel in the leaf — and once the leaf is warm and damp that same gel turns the surface slimy very quickly. No pantry figure is given and none should be assumed. Refrigerate the bunch unwashed as soon as you get home.
en.fridge: Store the leaves unwashed and loosely packed in a perforated bag in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and wash them only just before cooking. About 2–4 days is the working limit, borrowed from the published rule for tender salad greens, since no figure exists for Anredera cordifolia leaves themselves. Keeping them dry is more important here than with most greens: the leaves are mucilaginous and go slimy fast once wet, and a slimy leaf cannot be rinsed back.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for Madeira vine leaves and freezing them is not worth doing. The pleasure of the leaf is its texture — thick, tender and slightly slippery — and freezing bursts the cells, so what thaws is a dark green ooze. Nothing unsafe would happen, but nothing usable would come out either. These are best bought in the quantity you will cook that day.
spoilage: A slimy or slippery film across the leaves that rinsing does not remove
Leaves gone translucent, dark or water-soaked
Yellowing leaves, or stems that have gone soft and limp
A sour or fermented smell when the bag is opened
tips: Choose bunches with thick, firm, bright green leaves and no wet patches.
Store unwashed and loosely packed; wash just before cooking.
Stir-fry hot and fast with sesame oil, ginger and a little rice wine.
Pick the thicker stems out; the leaves cook in under a minute and the stems do not.

faq.q: How long do Madeira vine leaves last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, unwashed and loosely packed. That figure is borrowed from the rule for tender salad greens; none is published for this plant.

faq.q: Can you freeze Madeira vine leaves?
faq.a: There is no timeline and no point. Freezing bursts the cells and the thick, slightly slippery texture that is the whole appeal is lost entirely.
They are mucilaginous, containing a soluble gel much like okra or Malabar spinach. That is a feature in the wok, and also the reason they go slimy fast if stored wet.

faq.q: Can you eat Madeira vine leaves raw?
faq.a: They are normally cooked, briefly and hot. Raw leaves are edible but the mucilage is more noticeable and the flavour is flat.

zh.name: 川七
zh.summary: 川七是落葵薯（Anredera cordifolia）厚實、略帶黏滑的心形葉片，在台灣最常見的吃法是麻油薑絲快炒。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照嫩葉沙拉菜來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 2～4 天。
zh.pantry: 這種葉子沒有什麼可用的常溫保存期。它含黏質——下鍋後那股滑潤口感，就是葉子裡的可溶性膠質——而一旦葉片變溫又帶水，同樣的膠質就會讓表面很快變得黏滑。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請不清洗直接冷藏。
zh.fridge: 不清洗、鬆鬆裝進打洞袋，放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，要煮之前才洗。約 2～4 天是工作上限，這是比照嫩葉沙拉菜的公布規則而來，因為落葵薯葉本身沒有任何數據。保持乾燥在這裡比其他葉菜更重要：川七含黏質，一沾水就變黏得特別快，而已經變黏的葉子沖洗也救不回來。
zh.freezer: 川七沒有冷凍保存期限，冷凍也不值得。這種葉子的樂趣全在質地——厚實、柔嫩、略帶滑潤——而冷凍會撐破細胞，解凍後只剩一攤深綠色的黏液。這不會有安全問題，但也沒有任何能用的東西。川七請買當天就會煮完的份量。
spoilage: 葉面出現沖洗也去不掉的黏滑薄膜
葉子變得半透明、發暗或像泡過水
葉片泛黃，或莖變得軟塌
打開袋子聞到酸味或發酵味
tips: 挑葉片厚實挺硬、翠綠、沒有濕爛處的。
不清洗、鬆鬆裝袋保存，要煮之前才洗。
麻油、薑絲加一點米酒大火快炒。
把比較粗的莖挑掉；葉子不到一分鐘就熟，莖不會。

faq.q: 川七放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、不清洗鬆鬆裝袋，約 2～4 天。這個數字是比照嫩葉沙拉菜而來；這種植物本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，也沒有意義。冷凍會撐破細胞，那份厚實滑潤的口感會完全消失。
它含有黏質，跟秋葵或皇宮菜一樣有可溶性膠質。這在鍋裡是優點，但也正是它濕著保存會很快變黏的原因。
一般都是快炒吃熟的。生葉雖然可以吃，但黏感更明顯、味道也偏平淡。
